spots.name: University of al-Qarawiyyin
spots.summary: The University of al-Qarawiyyin, also written Al-Karaouine or Al Quaraouiyine, is a university located in Fez, Morocco. It was founded as a mosque by Fatima al-Fihri in 857–859 and subsequently became one of the leading spiritual and educational centers of the Islamic Golden Age.

spots.name: Royal Palace of Fez

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Royal Palace or Dar al-Makhzen is the palace of the King of Morocco in the city of Fez, Morocco. Its original foundation dates back to the foundation of Fes el-Jdid, the royal citadel of the Marinid dynasty, in 1276. Most of the palace today dates from the 'Alawi era.

spots.name: Bab Bou Jeloud
spots.summary: Bab Bou Jeloud is an ornate city gate in Fes el Bali, the old city of Fez, Morocco. The current gate was built by the French colonial administration in 1913 to serve as the grand entrance to the old city.

spots.name: Fes el Bali
spots.summary: Fes el Bali is the oldest part of Fez, Morocco. It is one of the three main districts of Fez, along with Fes Jdid and the French-created Ville Nouvelle.

spots.name: Bou Inania Madrasa
spots.summary: The Bou Inania Madrasa or Bu 'Inaniya Madrasa is a madrasa in Fez, Morocco, built in 1350–55 by the Marinid sultan Abu Inan Faris. It is the only madrasa in Morocco which also functioned as a congregational mosque.

spots.name: Al-Attarine Madrasa
spots.summary: The Al-Attarine Madrasa or Medersa al-Attarine is a madrasa in Fez, Morocco, near the Al-Qarawiyyin Mosque. It was built by the Marinid sultan Uthman II Abu Said between 1323 and 1325. The madrasa takes its name from the Souk al-Attarine, the spice and perfume market.

spots.name: Funduq al-Najjarin
spots.summary: Funduq al-Najjarin is a historic funduq in Fes el Bali, the old medina quarter in the city of Fez, Morocco.

spots.name: Chouara Tannery
spots.summary: Chouara Tannery is one of the three tanneries in the city of Fez, Morocco. It is the largest tannery in the city and one of the oldest. It is located in Fes el Bali, the oldest medina quarter of the city, near the Saffarin Madrasa along the Oued Fes.

spots.name: Zawiya of Moulay Idris II
spots.summary: The Zawiya of Moulay Idris II is a zawiya in Fez, Morocco. One of the holiest shrines in Morocco, it contains the tomb of Idris II, a sharif who ruled what is now Morocco from 807 to 828 and is traditionally considered the founder and patron saint of Fez.

spots.name: Marinid Tombs
spots.summary: The Marinid Tombs or Merenid Tombs are a set of ruined monumental tombs on a hill above and north of Fes al-Bali, the old city of Fez, Morocco. They were originally a royal necropolis for the Marinid dynasty which ruled over Morocco in the 13th to 15th centuries.

spots.name: Ibn Danan Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ibn Danan Synagogue is a synagogue located in the Mellah of Fez, Morocco. The first synagogue on the site was built in the 17th century but the building has been destroyed, partially or completely, and restored on several occasions. Most recently, the synagogue was reopened in 1999 after another restoration.

spots.name: Zawiya of Sidi Ahmed al-Tijani
spots.summary: The Zawiya of Sidi Ahmed al-Tijani is a zawiya in Fez, Morocco. It is dedicated to the 18th-century founder of the Tijaniyyah order, Sheikh Ahmad al-Tijani, who is buried here.

spots.name: Andalusian Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mosque of the Andalusians or Al-Andalusiyyin Mosque, sometimes also called the Andalusian Mosque, is a major historic mosque in Fes el Bali, the old medina quarter of Fez, Morocco. The mosque was founded in 859–860, making it one of the oldest mosques in Morocco.

spots.name: Bou Jeloud Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bou Jeloud Mosque is a historic Almohad-era mosque in the former Kasbah of Bou Jeloud, located near Bab Bou Jeloud, in Fez, Morocco.

spots.name: Saffarin Madrasa
spots.summary: Saffarin Madrasa is a madrasa in Fes el-Bali, the old medina quarter of Fez, Morocco. It was built in 1271 CE by the Marinid Sultan Abu Ya'qub Yusuf and was the first of many madrasas built by the Marinid dynasty during their reign.

spots.name: Al-Qarawiyyin Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The University of al-Qarawiyyin, also written Al-Karaouine or Al Quaraouiyine, is a university located in Fez, Morocco. It was founded as a mosque by Fatima al-Fihri in 857–859 and subsequently became one of the leading spiritual and educational centers of the Islamic Golden Age.

spots.name: Bab Mahrouk
spots.summary: Bab Mahrouk, also spelled Bab Mahruq, is historically the main western city gate of Fes el Bali, the old walled city of Fes, Morocco. The gate dates from 1204 and is located on the northwestern corner of Place Bou Jeloud, near the edge of Kasbah an-Nouar.

spots.name: Cherratine Madrasa
spots.summary: Cherratine Madrasa is a madrasa in Fez, Morocco. It is also known as the Er-Rachidia Madrasa or Ras al-Cherratine Madrasa. It was built in 1670 by the Alawi sultan Moulay al-Rashid.

spots.name: Sharabliyyin Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sharabliyyin Mosque is a historic mosque in Fez, Morocco. It was first built in the 14th century during the Marinid dynasty period and underwent a major restoration in the late 19th or early 20th century during the Alawi period.

spots.name: Place Seffarine
spots.summary: Place Seffarine or Seffarine Square is a small square in the medina of Fes, Morocco. It is located on the south side of the Qarawiyyin Mosque, close to the Bou Khrareb River which runs through the heart of the medina. The square dates back to the Middle Ages but has also undergone renovations in modern times.

spots.name: Maristan of Sidi Frej
spots.summary: The Maristan of Sidi Frej or Maristan of Fez was a historic maristan in Fez, Morocco. It was founded by the Marinids in the 13th century and functioned as a hospital and as a hospice for the destitute and mentally ill up until the 20th century.

spots.name: Abu al-Hasan Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mosque of Abu al-Hasan is a historic neighbourhood mosque in Fes el-Bali, the old medina of Fez, Morocco. It is located on Tala'a Seghira street, near the Bou Inania Madrasa.

spots.name: Kissariat al-Kifah
spots.summary: The Kissariat al-Kifah or Kissaria (القيسارية) is the historic central bazaar of Fes el-Bali, the historic old city of Fez, Morocco. It is located between the Zawiya of Moulay Idris II and the Qarawiyyin Mosque.

spots.name: R'cif Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The R'cif Mosque is a congregational mosque in Fes el-Bali, the old city (medina) of Fez, Morocco. It has one of the tallest minarets in the city and overlooks Place R'cif in the heart of the medina.

spots.name: Al Fassiyine Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Al Fassiyine Synagogue or Slat Al Fassiyine is a synagogue located in the Mellah of Fez, Morocco. Reputed to be one of the oldest synagogues in Fez, it was one of the few synagogues where the non-Sephardic rituals of the toshavim continued up until the 20th century.

spots.name: Tala'a Kebira
spots.summary: Tala'a Kebira is one of the longest and most important streets in Fes el-Bali, the old city (medina) of Fes, Morocco. The street runs roughly east to west, starting near the Bab Bou Jeloud and Bab Mahrouk gates in the west and ending at the al-Attarine Madrasa in the east, near the Qarawiyyin Mosque.

spots.name: Kasbah An-Nouar
spots.summary: The Kasbah An-Nouar or Kasbah Filali is a walled district and former military enclosure in the old medina of Fez, Morocco. Its name means "citadel of the flowers", but it is sometimes also referred to as Kasbah Filala and Kasbah Chorfa.

spots.name: Ain al-Kheil Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ain al-Kheil Mosque, also known as the al-Azhar Mosque, is a historic mosque in Fes el-Bali, the old medina of Fes, Morocco.

spots.name: Diwan Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Diwan Mosque is a mosque in Fez, Morocco. It was founded by the Alawi sultan Moulay Slimane during his reign between 1792 and 1822. It is located in the center of Fes el-Bali, on Diwan Street, just north of Tala'a Kebira near its eastern end. It is one of the neighbourhood Friday mosques of the city.

spots.name: Bab Guissa
spots.summary: Bab Guissa or Bab Gisa is the main northwestern gate of Fes el Bali, the old walled city of Fes, Morocco.

spots.name: Funduq al-Tetwaniyyin
spots.summary: Funduq al-Tetwaniyyin, also known as Funduq al-Staouniyine, is a historic funduq (caravanserai) in Fes el-Bali, the old city of Fes, Morocco.

spots.name: Mesbahiyya Madrasa
spots.summary: Mesbahiyya Madrasa is a madrasa in Fes el Bali, the old medina quarter in the city of Fez, Morocco. Its construction is dated to 1346, during the Marinid period. It is located next to the University of al-Qarawiyyin.

spots.name: Sidi Moussa Tannery
spots.summary: The Sidi Moussa Tannery or Guerniz Tannery is a historic tanning facility located in the heart of Fes el-Bali, the historic medina of Fez, Morocco. The tannery is located in the Guerniz neighbourhood, near the Zawiya of Moulay Idris II and the Nejjarine Museum.

spots.name: Bab al-Amer
spots.summary: Bab al-Amer is one of the historic city gates of Fez, Morocco. It was the southwestern entrance to Fes el-Jdid, the royal city founded in 1276 by the Marinids west of Fes el Bali.

spots.name: Mnebhi Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mnebhi Palace or Menebhi Palace, also known by its French name Palais Mnebhi, is a historic early 20th-century palace in Fes el-Bali, the old medina of Fes, Morocco. It is notable for both its lavish architecture as well as for being the place where the 1912 Treaty of Fes was officially signed.

spots.name: Bab Guissa Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bab Guissa Mosque is a medieval mosque in northern Fes el-Bali, the old city of Fez, Morocco. It is located next to the city gate of the same name, and also features an adjoining madrasa.

spots.name: El-Oued Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The El-Oued Mosque is a mosque in Fes el-Bali, the historic medina of Fez, Morocco. It was built in the late 18th or early 19th century on the site of a former 14th-century madrasa by the same name.

spots.name: Funduq Shamma'in
spots.summary: The Funduq al-Shamma'in or Foundouk Chemmaïne is a medieval funduq in Fes, Morocco. It is also directly adjoined by another funduq structure, the Funduq al-Sbitriyyin. Together, the two form a combined architectural complex sometimes referred to as the Funduq Shamma'in-Sbitriyyin.

spots.name: Bab Semmarine
spots.summary: Bab Semmarine is the monumental southern gate of Fes el-Jdid, a part of the old city of Fez, Morocco.

spots.name: Funduq Sagha
spots.summary: Funduq Sagha is a historic funduq in Fes el Bali, the old medina quarter in the city of Fez, Morocco.

spots.name: Sahrij Madrasa
spots.summary: The Sahrij Madrasa, also rendered as the Madrasa al-Sahrij or Sihrij Madrasa, is a madrasa in Fez, Morocco. It is located inside Fes el Bali, the old medina quarter of the city. The madrasa dates back to the 14th century during the golden age of Fez under Marinid rule.

spots.name: Place Bou Jeloud
spots.summary: Place Bou Jeloud, also known as Place Pacha el-Baghdadi, is a large public square in Fes, Morocco, located west of Bab Bou Jeloud gate.

spots.name: Sba'iyyin Madrasa
spots.summary: The Sba'iyyin Madrasa or Madrasa as-Sba'iyyin is a historic madrasa in the medina of Fez, Morocco. It is located in the Andalous quarter of Fes el-Bali, next to the Mosque of the Andalusians. It was founded in 1323 by Sultan Abu al-Hasan and adjoins the larger Sahrij Madrasa, which was founded just before it.
